caption: Open benchmark of the multifat library, regenerated whenever the library changes. Rows: criteria, by family; dots on the right mark those that need strains or use their own life law. Columns: materials with fatigue-life data. Colour: share of independent tests predicted within ±10 % of the load, or mean load error e_L. Select a cell for its statistics.
provenance: Output of multifat-pipeline --all (multiaxial-fatigue, commit %commit%), which calibrates and runs every registered criterion on each workbook. e_L = ln(1/s*), where s* scales the load history until the calibrated criterion predicts the observed life; e_L > 0 is conservative. Only failures not used for calibration are counted; run-outs and fatigue-limit-only workbooks are excluded. Test data come from the published sources listed in the repository's PROVENANCE.md.

metric_items: For each test, s* is the factor that, applied to the whole load history (means included), makes the calibrated criterion predict exactly the observed life: e_L = ln(1/s*).

e_L = 0 is an exact prediction. e_L = +0.10 means the criterion matches the observed life only at about 0.90 × the applied load: it judges the test more severe than it was (conservative). e_L = −0.10 is the non-conservative counterpart.

Unlike a life error, e_L does not grow with the flatness of the S–N curve or with the power of the load in the damage parameter (squared for SWT and the energy criteria), so every criterion is measured on the same scale.
Within ±10 %: share of tests with |1/s* − 1| ≤ 0.10. Mean e_L is the systematic bias; its standard deviation is the scatter.

Only failures not used to calibrate the criterion or its S–N curve are counted; run-outs give bounds only and are excluded. Independence from constants supplied with the data, such as fatigue limits, is not yet traced (multifat issue #14).

Complexity is shown beside the score, not folded into it: whether the criterion needs strains (E, ν) besides stresses, whether it uses its own life law instead of a calibrated master curve DP = A·Nᵇ, and which material constants it requires (* optional).
legend_facet: ε: needs strain · N: native life law
